Turn 32. Solves 49/50 (this revert is a free re-simulation of already-evaluated settings). FINAL: R1303-style 2-column low-pressure cascade = reward 1.205, the best valid design evaluated.

ANCHOR (my best): '' 40/3.0/3.0/0.8 -> T (1601 mol/s C3/C4/C5 mush, $0) + B; 'B' 50/6.0/6.0/0.8 -> BT 910 mol/s = 97% C6-paraffin mix, sells $1067.1M/yr; BB 789 mol/s C7/C8/cyclo, $0. Cost $538.7M/yr. Reward (1067.1-538.7)/439 = 1.205.

EVIDENCE: (1) LOW PRESSURE (dp=0.8, ~5 bar) sharpens volatilities cheaply - the whole winning cut is done with just 40/3 and 50/6. (2) Every extra column on T or BB lost money: T-split cols cost $685-1273M/yr for worthless C4/C5 mush (best TB 88% C5, needs 95%); BB col (agent-34 R1448, 60/12) cost $111M and gave 45% cyclo/31% nC7 - worthless. A 3rd column must clear ~$250-290M/yr and none can. (3) High column counts at 24 bar always lose.

DECISION: bank 1.205. No budget left for further gambles worth taking; finishing at the known optimum.
